findings.title: Spawned workers fail the process type check and are never killed
findings.body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, whose SpawnProcess class is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process. This isinstance check therefore returns false for production workers, skipping kill() before starting a replacement. A hung worker remains alive and can resume flushing the same shards concurrently with its replacement, causing duplicate production and leaking processes across restarts. The same check in join() also skips termination. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the actual spawn-context process class instead.

findings.title: Terminate remaining workers after the join deadline expires
findings.body: When next_step.join() or an earlier worker consumes the shutdown timeout, this break skips every remaining worker, including their termination logic. Setting the shared stopped flag does not interrupt a worker blocked in Redis or future.result(), so those workers can survive a rebalance and later flush shards now owned by another consumer. Once the deadline expires, stop waiting but still terminate and reap all remaining workers.
